thread.title: Fed Chairman Powell Sees Fed Rates 'Just Below' Neutral; Dow Jones Soars | Investor's Business Daily

author: ED CARSON
title: Fed Chairman Powell Sees Fed Rates 'Just Below' Neutral; Dow Jones Soars | Investor's Business Daily
text:
Federal Reserve chief Jerome Powell said Wednesday that interest rates are "just below" neutral, hinting at a more-dovish turn on Fed rate hikes. The Dow Jones, S&P 500 index and Nasdaq composite boomed on Powell's comments, which suggest fewer Fed rate hikes going forward. The comments come a day after President Trump stepped up his criticism of his pick as Fed chairman.
X Fed Rates 'Just Below' Neutral "Interest rates are still low by historical standards, and they remain just below the broad range of estimates of the level that would be neutral for the economy — that is, neither speeding up nor slowing down growth," Powell told the Economic Club of New York in a speech.
In early October, Powell had said that Fed rates were a "long way off" from neutral.
The Fed chairman said he and fellow policymakers remain upbeat on the U.S. economy, "forecasting continued solid growth, low unemployment, and inflation near 2%."

"We also know that the economic effects of our gradual rate increases are uncertain, and may take a year or more to be fully realized," he said. "While FOMC participants' projections are based on our best assessments of the outlook, there is no preset policy path."
Dow Jones Spikes On Fed Chairman Powell The Dow Jones rose 2.5% in the stock market after Fed Chairman Powell spoke. The S&P 500 index climbed 2.3% and the Nasdaq composite nearly 3%. The Dow Jones reclaimed its 200-day moving average. The Nasdaq composite, in day five of a rally attempt, is looking for a follow-through day to confirm a new uptrend.
Microsoft ( MSFT ) and Apple ( AAPL ) stock, both members of the Dow Jones, S&P 500 and Nasdaq, both spiked nearly 4%. Microsoft stock, which reclaimed its 50-day line, is vying to overtake Apple stock as the world's most valuable company.
The 10-year Treasury yield fell about 2 basis points to 3.04%. The two-year Treasury yield fell 4 basis points to 2.80%. The U.S. dollar fell, easing pressure on U.S. multinationals' profits and some emerging markets.
Powell Speech Follows Trump Criticism President Trump had been increasingly vocal about Fed rate hikes, telling the Washington Post in an interview published late Tuesday that he's not "even a little bit happy with my selection" as Fed chairman. He said the Federal Reserve is a "bigger problem than China."
Trump's public pressure could actually spur Powell and other policymakers to stay on their Fed rate hike path to stake out their independence from the White House.
Markets Not Pricing In Multiple Fed Rate Hikes In 2019 But financial markets appear to agree that Trump has a point with regards to Fed rate hikes, given the current stock market correction and signs of slowing economic growth in the U.S. and overseas. The stock market worry has been that the Fed will be raising rates into 2019, as tax and spending stimulus wear off and Trump trade wars have a deeper impact.
Before Fed Chairman Powell spoke, markets saw a 75% chance of a Fed rate hike next month. After Powell's comments, that rose to about 83%.
But for 2019, investors have only fully priced in one Fed rate hike in 2019, with only a 32% chance of a second hike by year-end. That's down slightly from 37% before Powell. Fed policymakers have been projecting three Fed rate hikes next year.
On Tuesday, Federal Vice Chairman Richard Clarida was the latest policymaker to give mixed signals. He backed gradual Fed rate hikes but wouldn't say how many.
